content: 1. Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nabumetone: Co-administration of these drugs can increase each other's toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Toxicity may occur when emtricitabine and tenofovir are combined with other drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, such as high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 2. Nafcillin and Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Nafcillin decreases the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 3. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Naldemedine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases naldemedine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Naloxegol: This combination is contraindicated as elvitegravir/cobicistat increases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing opioid withdrawal symptoms. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Naproxen: Co-administration may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 6. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nateglinide: Elvitegravir decreases nateglinide levels by inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely as elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. 7. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nebivolol: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases nebivolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, as cobicistat is a CYP2D6 inhibitor. Elevated plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates may lead to serious or life-threatening events. 8. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nefazodone: This combination increases nefazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Nefazodone also increases elvitegravir/cobicistat levels, necessitating caution. 9. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nelfinavir: Co-administration is contraindicated as nelfinavir increases elvitegravir/cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This may lead to significant adverse effects. Use alternative drugs. 10. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Neomycin: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nevirapine: This combination is contraindicated as nevirapine reduces elvitegravir/cobicistat levels, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 12. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nicardipine: Elvitegravir/cobicistat increases nicardipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 13. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nifedipine: Co-administration increases nifedipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 14. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nilotinib: This combination increases nilotinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 15. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nimodipine: Co-administration increases nimodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 16. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nirogacestat: This combination is contraindicated as it increases nirogacestat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use alternative drugs. 17. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nisoldipine: Co-administration increases nisoldipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 18. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Norgestimate: This combination increases norgestimate levels, potentially causing insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, acne, and venous thrombosis. It also decreases ethinyl estradiol levels, reducing contraceptive efficacy. Monitor closely. 19. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Norgestrel: Co-administration increases norgestrel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Nortriptyline: This combination is contraindicated as it increases nortriptyline levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Use alternative drugs. 21. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Olaparib: Co-administration increases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute capsules with tablets. 22. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Oliceridine: Co-administration increases oliceridine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 23. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Omaveloxolone: This combination is contraindicated as it increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely. 24. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Omeprazole: No clinically significant interactions are expected based on studies with Stribild components. 25. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ondansetron: Co-administration increases ondansetron levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 26. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Osimertinib: This combination is contraindicated as it increases osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration. 27. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ospemifene: Co-administration increases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Oxaliplatin: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Oxaprozin: Co-administration may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 30. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Oxcarbazepine: This combination is contraindicated as oxcarbazepine reduces elvitegravir/cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 31. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Oxycodone: Co-administration increases oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 32. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Paclitaxel: Co-administration increases paclitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 33. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Pacritinib: This combination is contraindicated as it increases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use alternative drugs. 34. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Palbociclib: Co-administration increases palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day if unavoidable. 35. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Palovarotene: This combination is contraindicated as it increases palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use alternative drugs. 36. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Panobinostat: Co-administration increases panobinostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if co-administered. 37. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Pantoprazole: No clinically significant interactions are expected based on studies with Stribild components. 38. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Paricalcitol: Co-administration increases paricalcitol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 39. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Paromomycin: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Paroxetine: Co-administration increases paroxetine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 41. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Pazopanib: Co-administration increases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 42. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Pentamidine: Co-administration increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Pentobarbital: This combination is contraindicated as pentobarbital reduces elvitegravir/cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 44. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Perphenazine: Co-administration increases perphenazine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. A dose reduction of the neuroleptic may be needed. 45. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Phenobarbital: This combination is contraindicated as phenobarbital reduces elvitegravir/cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance.
